function.uniprot_function: Acts as a negative regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway by promoting the degradation of beta-catenin. Down-regulates beta-catenin by acting as a scaffold protein for the beta-catenin destruction complex, which phosphorylates beta-catenin, leading to its ubiquitination and degradation. AXIN2 probably facilitates the phosphorylation of CTNNB1 and APC by GSK3B. Itself is a transcriptional target of the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, creating a negative feedback loop. When constitutively localized to the nucleus, alters the chromatin structure at the MYC promoter and directly represses MYC gene expression.
function.tissue_specificity: Ubiquitous expression with low tissue specificity (Tau=0.30). Expression enhanced in colorectal cancer due to Wnt pathway activation. Medium expression in hepatocytes and low brain regional specificity.

Positive regulation of protein kinase activity

pathways.pathway_role_summary: AXIN2 is a scaffold protein in the beta-catenin destruction complex, coordinating GSK3B and CK1A1 kinases to phosphorylate beta-catenin for proteasomal degradation. It serves as a negative regulator of Wnt signaling and is itself a transcriptional target of the pathway, creating a negative feedback loop. AXIN2 turnover is regulated by tankyrase-mediated PARsylation followed by RNF146 ubiquitination, and by SIAH1-mediated ubiquitination.

disease_associations.description: Autosomal dominant syndrome caused by AXIN2 mutations (e.g., R656X). Features include severe tooth agenesis (oligodontia) and predisposition to colorectal polyps and early-onset colorectal cancer.
AXIN2 variants associated with increased colorectal cancer risk. Gene located in 17q23-q24 region showing frequent loss of heterozygosity in multiple tumor types.
Isolated tooth agenesis without cancer predisposition associated with AXIN2 variants. AXIN2 is one of the most common genes mutated in familial tooth agenesis.

metadata.data_quality_notes: High-quality data with multiple crystal structures for individual domains (RGS, DIX, beta-catenin binding). Some PTM sites (especially phosphorylation) differ between AXIN1 and AXIN2 - CK1α phosphorylation site conserved in AXIN1 but not AXIN2. Kinetic data limited to binding affinities (Kd values) for tankyrase and GSK3B; catalytic parameters (Kcat, Km) not extensively reported. Most interaction studies do not distinguish between AXIN1 and AXIN2. Isoform 2 sequence not fully characterized.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: AXIN2 is a critical scaffold in Wnt signaling with well-defined binding sites for multiple partners. Key for modeling: (1) Sequential phosphorylation mechanism - CK1A1 primes beta-catenin followed by GSK3B; (2) Negative feedback loop - AXIN2 expression induced by Wnt pathway it inhibits; (3) Degradation regulation via tankyrase-RNF146 and SIAH1 pathways; (4) Phase separation and polymerization via DIX domain affects activity; (5) Nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling adds spatial regulation. Quantitative binding data available for tankyrase (Kd ~1-5 μM) and GSK3B (Kd ~3 μM). AXIN2 shows non-redundant functions compared to AXIN1 in destruction complex formation.
